## Summary

mlx-rs is a Rust binding and high-level framework for Apple's MLX machine learning framework, designed to run on Apple Silicon hardware via the Metal GPU API. The repository is organized as a Cargo workspace containing several interdependent crates: a core array/operations library (mlx-rs, likely wrapping the C++ MLX library via FFI), procedural macro crates (mlx-internal-macros, mlx-macros) that provide derive macros and builder-pattern code generation for neural network modules, LLM utility crates (mlx-lm-utils for tokenization and chat template rendering via Jinja2, mlx-lm for model loading and text generation pipelines), and runnable example binaries demonstrating MNIST training and LLM inference with models such as Mistral and Qwen3. The crates form a layered dependency stack: macros are consumed by the core library, the core library is consumed by the LLM utilities, and all layers are consumed by example applications. Externally, two downstream repositories ('inference' and 'LensWorks') are observed to call into mlx-rs extensively, indicating it is used as a dependency for Apple Silicon ML inference workloads. The project provides neural network primitives (convolutions, attention, transformers, activations), KV-cache management, quantization support, and streaming token generation, making it a Rust-native toolkit for on-device LLM inference and training on Apple hardware.

## Projects

### mlx-rs

mlx-rs is a Rust binding and high-level framework for Apple's MLX machine learning framework, targeting Apple Silicon hardware. The project provides neural network primitives (convolutions, transformers, activations), procedural macros for code generation and builder patterns, language model inference utilities (tokenization, chat template rendering, model loading), and example applications demonstrating MNIST training and LLM inference with models like Mistral and Qwen3. It is organized into a core array/ops library (pmetal-mlx-rs), macro crates (mlx-internal-macros, mlx-macros), LLM utilities (mlx-lm-utils, mlx-lm), and runnable examples.
